# dataiku_global_api_key (Resource)

A global API key on a Dataiku DSS instance. Requires an API key with admin rights.

DSS shows a key's secret once, when the key is created. This resource keeps it in `key`, which means **the secret is stored in Terraform state**. Protect the state accordingly. A key that was imported has no `key`, because DSS will not give the secret out again.

A key takes its rights in one of two ways, chosen with `groups`. Without `groups` the key carries its own rights, set with `admin` and `permissions`. With `groups` it has whatever those groups have and none of its own.

The provider still needs a key to start with. Create that first one by hand or with `dsscli api-key-create`, then use this resource for every key after it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A key for a deployment pipeline, carrying its own rights.
resource "dataiku_global_api_key" "ci" {
  label       = "ci"
  description = "Used by the deployment pipeline"

  # A new key is not empty-handed: DSS turns several abilities on by default,
  # mayCreateProjects among them. Name the ones you care about, in either
  # direction. The rest keep whatever the instance gave them.
  permissions = {
    mayCreateProjects  = true
    mayWriteUnsafeCode = false
  }
}

# A key that takes its rights from groups and expires after ninety days.
# The lifetime is counted from when the key is created.
resource "dataiku_global_api_key" "reporting" {
  label         = "reporting"
  groups        = ["readers"]
  lifetime_days = 90
}

# DSS shows the secret once, at creation, and this is the only place to read
# it afterwards. It is stored in state, so keep the state somewhere private.
output "ci_api_key" {
  value     = dataiku_global_api_key.ci.key
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `admin` (Boolean) Whether the key has DSS administrator rights. Cannot be set together with `groups`.
- `description` (String) What the key is for.
- `groups` (Set of String) Names of the groups the key takes its rights from. Every group must exist. Setting this, even to an empty set, makes the key group-based: it has no `admin` flag and no `permissions` of its own.

Adding `groups` to an existing key changes it in place and keeps its secret. Removing `groups` altogether forces a new key with a new secret, because DSS refuses to turn a group-based key back into one with its own rights.
- `label` (String) A short name for the key, shown in the DSS key list. DSS does not require labels to be unique.
- `lifetime_days` (Number) How many days the key lasts. `0`, the default, means it does not expire.

DSS counts from when the key was created, not from when this was last changed, so setting `7` on a key made a month ago gives an expiry date in the past.
- `permissions` (Map of Boolean) Global abilities granted to the key, keyed by the raw DSS field name. The names are the ones `dataiku_group` takes in its own `permissions`, for example `mayCreateProjects` or `mayWriteUnsafeCode`. Cannot be set together with `groups`.

A new key is not empty-handed. DSS 15 turns these on by default: `mayCreateProjects`, `mayWriteInRootProjectFolder`, `mayCreateActiveWebContent`, `mayCreateDataCollections`, `mayPublishToDataCollections` and `mayShareToWorkspaces`. Set them to `false` here for a key that should not have them.

Abilities absent from this map are left at whatever the instance has. A name the instance does not know is refused, because DSS would otherwise drop it and report success.
- `user_for_impersonation` (String) Login of the DSS user associated with the key, the field DSS calls `dssUserForImpersonation`. DSS stores whatever is given here without checking that the user exists.

### Read-Only

- `expires_on` (String) When the key expires, as an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC. Null when the key does not expire.
- `id` (String) The identifier DSS gives the key. This is not the secret.
- `key` (String, Sensitive) The secret, as DSS returned it when the key was created. Stored in state. Null for an imported key.

The secret never changes while the key exists. To rotate it, replace the resource: `terraform apply -replace=dataiku_global_api_key.NAME`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Keys are imported by their id, not by their secret or their label. The id is
# the "id" field of each entry that GET /public/api/admin/global-api-keys/
# returns.
#
# An imported key has no secret in state: DSS gives it out once, when the key
# is created, and masks it on every read after that. Abilities are tracked
# only for the names the configuration's permissions map lists.
terraform import dataiku_global_api_key.ci Ab3dEf6hIj9kLm2n
```
